text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatian government initiates endorsement of the European Council's conventions on money laundering, torture and inhumane punishment and protection of national mionority rights.

- Deputy Foreign Minister Ivo Sanader met U.S. assistant secretary of state for human rights John Shattuck. They discussed future steps to boost the Bosnian federation and normalise relations with Belgrade.
- Social liberal party HSLS in the coastal town of Sibenik expelled a dozen prominent members for voting for a coalition with the ruling HDZ in the city government.
- Slavonski Brod, placed at vital crossings into Bosnia and with good railway connections, will soon take steps to become a free trade zone, says head of the local chamber of economy Kresimir Rudec.
- Zagreb will no longer be a town of heavy industry and good public transport will allow limiting car traffic in the town's centre within three years, mayor Marina Dropulic Matulovic says.
- Zagrebacka Banka is currently replacing some 12,000 Euro and Master cards to add new safety codes.
- State telecoms recently closed down 14 local radio and three TV stations for failing to pay for their frequency use. All but one found money to pay debts and had reopened within days.
- Zagreb zoo acquired red panda bears from the southern Himalayas for the first time in 17 years.
- Tourism Minister Niko Bulic says he is proud and surprised to hear that his wife is the author of the new and heavily criticised tourist slogan 'Croatia-paradise on Earth'.
- Croatian ambassador to the Holy See denies allegations that some 200 million Swiss francs in gold looted from Jewish families during Croatia's fascist state in 1943, is hidden in Vatican banks.
- "I am against those who dream of chaos," says Drazen Budisa, former head of Social democratic party, now seen as the leader of its faction which favours coalition with the ruling HDZ.
- Shipper Atlantska Plovidba may take over the renovation and become the majority owner of Imperial, the oldest hotel in Dubrovnik.
- Famous Spanish tenor Placido Domingo is scheduled to sing in Split on August 12. A special stage including 4,500 seats will be built for the occasion. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
